text.p: COR Therapeutics Inc said Friday the application for European marketing approval of Integrilin as an adjunct therapy to prevent acute cardiac ischemic complications in patients undergoing percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty was withdrawn.
It said the withdrawal was based on discussions with European regulatory authorities and Schering-Plough Corp, COR's worldwide partner for the Intergrilin product.

Additional clinical results for the antithrombotic injection are expected to be available later this year from Pursuit, a 10,900 patient Phase III trial of Integrilin for use in unstable angina and non-Q wave myocardial infarction, the company explained.
It said these results could form the basis for an application for marketing approval of Integrilin.

COR said the withdrawn application was submitted last year by Schering-Plough to the European Agency for the Evaluation of Medicinal Products, the central regulatory agency for several European countries, and was based on the results of the IMPACT II study announced in 1995.
